title: Risks of Cultural Erasure in Large Language Models
benchmark_measurement: The benchmark measured the representation of different global regions in LLM-generated travel recommendations in response to queries about 'spiritual' journeys and the presence of religious themes in generated descriptions of cities.
findings: The study found that LLMs reproduce cultural stereotypes by simplifying regional representations. For instance, Southern Asia was well-represented only in queries related to spiritual experiences, and East Asia was framed as a destination for 'spiritual awakening,' which the authors note continues Western colonial tropes. This indicates a form of cultural erasure where complex regions are reduced to a single, often spiritual, dimension.
references: Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie. The danger of a single story, 2009.
